info.title: emuled
info.description: REST/JSON API of the eMule daemon for Linux. By default it listens only on 127.0.0.1; every call (except /ping and /openapi.json) requires "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN".

code.description: Stable code (for example not_found, bad_hash, kad_unavailable): it does not change with the language or with the text; the interface translates it

NewDownload.description: One of the two forms: link, or hash+name+size

sources_other_files.description: users who also have this file but whom eMule is using for another download (A4AF): they do not count in sources

best_queue_rank.description: closest queue position among all sources; 0 = no source in queue

file_op.description: operation in progress on the file: hash verification, copy, decompression, import of parts

file_op_percent.description: progress of the operation, 0-100 (0 if file_op is none)

completed_at.description: only for completed ones: time (Unix seconds)

path.description: only for completed ones: where the file is

query.description: Same syntax as eMule's search field (quotes, OR, NOT, ...)

answers.description: how many servers/nodes it came from

result_count.description: raw answers (one file can be counted several times)

part_file.description: it is a download still in progress

queued.description: clients in the queue for this file

indexed.description: Kad indexes hosted by us (with Kad running)

published.description: shared files announced to Kad at least once (with Kad running)

Preferences.description: eMule's preferences, grouped by page in APIDOC.md section 9. Only the keys to change are sent with PATCH.

incoming_path.description: folder for completed files (empty = the default one)

priority.description: 0 low, 1 normal, 2 high, 3 highest, 4 very low, 5 automatic

auto_cat.description: words that assign the category to new downloads

other_file.description: only for A4AF sources: the download for which eMule is using them right now

shared_missing.description: (read-only) shared folders that do not exist on disk: they stay in the list until you remove them

temp.description: where the .part files are; at least one

source.description: server = messages from the ed2k servers; api = actions done via API

last_id.description: number of the last line that existed: pass it as after the next time

truncated.description: with after: some lines between after and the first one left have already been discarded

upnp.description: UPnP (automatic opening of the ports on the router)

state.description: off = switched off; offline = the daemon has no network; pending = looking for the router; forwarded = ports forwarded; failed = the router did not forward them

version.description: eMule version announced on the network

base_version.description: eMule code that emuled derives from

get.description: The only call without a token: the web interface uses it to know whether the daemon is running.
Without a token. This way the interface knows whether to show the login or the first start.

post.description: Without a token but with the setup code (the token in the emuled.token file, printed by the daemon at startup until an account exists). Random salt + PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256; the password cannot be recovered, it is reset with emuled --reset-user.

username.description: 1-32 characters: letters, digits, dot, hyphen, underscore

post.summary: Log in with user name and password
post.description: Without a token. Answers with a session token (30 days), to be used as Bearer. Five wrong attempts from one address block it for one minute.

get.summary: Is the first start still to be completed?
get.description: pending=true after the first account is created, until the web Wizard is finished.

post.description: Marks the first start as completed (pending=false).

get.summary: Can an eMule profile be imported?
get.description: available=true only during the first start (Wizard not finished) and if nothing has been imported yet; imported=true after the import. candidates: folders on the computer that look like an eMule configuration (old ~/.emuled* installations, ~/.config/emule, ~/eMule/config, Wine, /mnt, /media), only if available.

post.description: Copies (the source folder is not modified) the configuration files of an eMule, usually a Windows one: user hash, key, credits, known files, servers, Kad nodes, preferences. Fixes the Windows paths with the given (or proposed) rules. The files are staged and the daemon restarts by itself: at startup it puts them in place (replaced files go into pre-import-DATE/). Only during the first start.

200.description: Staged; the daemon restarts in less than a second

409.description: It is not the first start, or something has already been imported

422.description: Invalid folder, not enough space or wrong rules

post.summary: Look at an eMule profile to import
post.description: Read-only. Lists the files that would be copied, the user name, the folders (Incoming, Temp, shared) and proposes the rules for Windows paths (e.g. Z:/eMule = /mnt/z/eMule) by looking above the given folder. With rules it recomputes where the folders would end up.

409.description: It is not the first start

422.description: It does not look like an eMule folder, it is the emuled one, or wrong rules

get.summary: Address of the emule-project.net port test
get.description: Like eMule's TriggerPortTest: https://porttest.emule-project.net/connectiontest.php with the TCP and UDP ports IN USE right now, lang (Windows language identifier: 1040 Italian, 1033 English; default 1033) and obf=0, or obf=1 and clienthash=<user hash> if obfuscation is on. The daemon does NOT open the address: the browser opens it when the user clicks; the site tries to connect to the ports and the daemon answers.

post.description: The daemon shuts down cleanly (saves everything) and starts again by itself, same process and same arguments (execv); needed for new ports. It answers at once and restarts in less than a second. The interface waits for it to come back and reloads the page.

501.description: Restart not available in this mode

get.description: Tries to listen (TCP) or to open (UDP) the given ports, then closes them. own=true: it is the port emuled already uses (no conflict). Changes nothing.

get.summary: Subfolders of a folder on the daemon's computer
get.description: For the 'choose a folder' window. These are the folders of the computer where the daemon runs (with Docker: of the container). Folders only, never files; hidden ones only with hidden=1; at most 2000. Without path it starts from the user's home folder.

400.description: Path not absolute or not a folder (bad_path, not_a_directory)

post.description: Creates ONE folder; the folder that contains it must exist.

404.description: The containing folder does not exist (dir_not_found)

get.description: Version, ports, connection to the ed2k server and to Kad, speeds and number of transfers.
All the files being downloaded (and those paused or stopped), in queue order.

post.description: By ed2k link ("link") or by "hash" + "name" + "size". The file starts at once unless it was chosen to add new ones paused.

400.description: The body is not a JSON object

409.description: The file is already being downloaded

post.description: Removes all completed downloads from the list (the files stay on disk). The list of completed ones is only in memory, like the eMule window: it is emptied when the daemon restarts. With the remove_finished_downloads option the completed ones never enter the list.

Resets the wait between source requests: on the next round the daemon asks the ed2k server and Kad for them at once (normally the server is queried every 15 minutes and Kad up to 1 hour per attempt). It answers at once (202); the sources appear gradually. If you are not connected to the networks it says so (server/kad = false).

server.description: connected to the server: the request will go out

paused.description: the download is stopped: sources are searched when it restarts

wait_s.description: the server accepts one group of source requests every 300 s: in how many seconds the queued one goes out (0 = now)

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

get.description: The known sources for the file, with the state of each one (downloading, queued, connecting, ...).

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

post.description: Creates a temporary link (valid 6 hours, for ONE file) that a local player such as VLC or mpv opens without the token. Response: path (to append to the daemon's address), name, size, mime, expires_in. For a download in progress it also turns on the preview priority (first and last part first). It also works for completed ones.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

get.description: Serves the file with range requests (Range, 206 response). It does not need the token: the authorization is the id in the path. For a download in progress only what is already on disk is served: if the requested range starts in a part not downloaded yet it answers 503 with Retry-After (the player retries), and a range that goes beyond the bytes present is shortened. 403 if the link is expired or unknown; 416 for an invalid range.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the name only, for players: it does not matter

get.description: The blocks (chunks of part_size = 9 728 000 bytes) that are arriving right now: for each one part (from 0), size, missing and the sources transferring it (name, software, ip, port, speed in bytes/s) with the pieces of block_size = 184 320 bytes requested (start, end, transferred). receiving = it is really arriving (false = only requested). Empty active list if no source is transferring. 404 if the download does not exist or is completed.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

get.summary: File names used by the sources
get.description: eMule's "Name" tab: the names by which the sources call the file, with how many sources use each one (most common first), and the current name (current). Empty list if no source has answered yet. 404 if the download does not exist or is already completed.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

get.description: eMule's "All comments" tab: comments and ratings (1 fake ... 5 excellent) received from the sources (network ed2k) and the notes found on Kad (network kad), with kad_connected, kad_searching and the anti-spam filter in use (filter).

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

post.description: Asks Kad for the other users' notes about this file (the "Search in Kad" button). The results arrive gradually and are read with GET .../comments.

409.description: A notes search for this file is already running

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

get.description: What eMule's "General" tab shows: name and .part.met file, ed2k and AICH hash (with the state: error, empty, untrusted, trusted, verified, complete), available hashsets, size and space on disk, total and available parts, sources (total, useful, transferring, without useful parts, used for another file), speed, transferred data, compression saved, completed, corrupted, remaining, parts recovered by I.C.H. and the dates (added, active time, last seen complete, last reception). Percentages truncated to the tenth, like eMule.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

get.description: state: idle (never requested), running, done, failed or unavailable. When the reading is finished (done): recognized, general {format, size, duration_s, overall_bitrate, title, movie, date}, video[] {codec, profile, codec_id, bitrate, width, height, aspect, fps, lang, title}, audio[] {codec, commercial, bitrate, channels, sampling, lang, title, default}, text[] (subtitles) {codec, lang, title, default, forced}. failed has reason (timeout, bad_output, spawn); unavailable has reason not_installed.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

post.description: Runs mediainfo on the file (the .part of a download in progress, or the file of a completed one) and answers at once (202); the result is read with GET. If mediainfo is not installed it answers 200 with state unavailable.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

get.description: The blocks (chunks) of 9 728 000 bytes: for each one how many bytes are missing, in how many sources it is available, the state (empty, partial, complete, corrupted) and verified (false = complete but cannot be checked: the hashset is missing); plus hashset at the top level.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

get.description: The templates found in /usr/share/emuled/templates (system), ~/.emuled/templates (user) and in the extra folder --templates-dir (dev), including invalid ones with the reason (errors). For each one: id, name, version, description, author, license, api, source, valid, errors, reserved, dir_name, url (/t/<id>/) and preview. dirs says where they are searched; api_version is the version of the templates the daemon understands. The choice of template lives only in the browser.

post.description: To be used after copying or removing a template. It answers with the same list as GET /templates.

get.description: The lines the daemon writes (connections to servers, errors, actions done via API: "[api] ..."). Without "after" it returns the last "limit" lines; with "after" only those newer than that number, to follow the log in pieces. Debug lines are present only with the verbose_log preference.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: number of the last line already seen

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: from 1 to 2000 (default 500)

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: minimum level (default info)

delete.description: Removes all the lines. Numbering continues.

get.description: The folder for completed files (incoming), the temporary folders for .part files and the shared folders.

put.description: Body with one or more fields: incoming, temp, shared. Everything is checked first (absolute paths, writable or readable folders, no duplicates) and nothing changes if there is an error. The temporary and incoming folders are created if missing; .part files already started stay where they are. When shared changes the daemon re-checks the shared files. "saved": written to the profile (only with the profile's identity and ports).

get.description: State of a download.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

patch.description: Body: "category" (id of a category), "priority" (auto, very_low, low, normal, high, release) and/or "name" (new file name: not empty, without "/", at most 255 bytes; it applies at once and also when the download is completed; 409 if the file is being verified or completed).

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

delete.description: Removes the download from the queue and DELETES the partial file (.part and .part.met). It cannot be undone.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

post.description: Stops the transfers but keeps the sources.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

post.description: Resumes a paused or stopped download.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

post.description: Stops the download and discards the sources (it resumes with resume and a new search).

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

get.description: All the search tabs, the most recent first, without the results (read them with GET /searches/{id}).

post.description: scope: "server" (only the connected server), "all" (also all the other servers, via UDP), "kad" (Kademlia network) or "global" (ed2k of all servers + Kad together, results merged by hash; it is enough that one of the two networks is connected). Only one search runs at a time: a new one stops the previous one. Searches are tabs: they stay with their results, even after a daemon restart (<config>/searches.json), until they are removed with DELETE. It answers at once (202); the results are read with GET /searches/{id}.

400.description: The body is not a JSON object

409.description: Not connected (to the ed2k server, or to Kad)

post.description: Repeats the same search (same word, same where and same filters) in the same tab: same id, the results start again from scratch. Like POST /searches, it stops the search that was running.

409.description: Not connected (to the ed2k server, or to Kad)

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Search number, returned by POST /searches

post.description: Stops the running search; the tab and the results already received stay.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Search number, returned by POST /searches

get.description: The results arrive gradually: poll until state is "finished". Equal files (same hash) from different servers are merged; sorted by number of sources.

404.description: Unknown search or removed from memory

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Search number, returned by POST /searches

delete.description: Stops the search if it is running and removes the tab, for good: it is the only way it goes away.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Search number, returned by POST /searches

get.description: The addresses (server.met) already used, the most recent first (file AC_ServerMetURLs.dat, the same as eMule), plus those of addresses.dat.
state: idle (never started), running, done (added = new servers, total = overall) or failed (error).

post.summary: Update the server list from an address
post.description: Downloads a server.met from an http or https address (certificate verified, at most 8 MB and 60 s, up to 5 redirects) and MERGES it into the list: new servers are added, nothing is removed. It answers at once (202); the outcome is read with GET. The address that worked is remembered.

400.description: The body is not a JSON object

get.description: state: idle, running, done (url: added = new contacts, contacts = overall) or failed (error).

post.summary: Repopulate Kad from a nodes.dat or from a node
post.description: With "url" it downloads a nodes.dat (http or https) and adds its contacts (Kad starts if it was off); with "address" (ip:port) it asks that node for the first contacts. One of the two, not both. With "url" it answers at once (202) and the outcome is read with GET.

400.description: The body is not a JSON object

409.description: Kad not available, already connected (with address) or a bootstrap in progress

address.description: ip:UDP port of a Kad node

get.description: All the files the daemon offers to others (shared folders and downloads in progress).

post.description: Re-reads the folders and computes the hash of new files. It answers at once (202).
How far ahead the file goes in the queue of whoever asks for it.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: MD4 of the file: 32 hexadecimal characters

get.description: Who is downloading from you right now and who is waiting in the queue.
Connection, firewall, contacts and estimated users.

post.description: Starts (or restarts) Kad with the profile's nodes.dat. Connecting takes a few tens of seconds: the status is read from /kad. 409 if the daemon has no Kad (--no-kad and --offline) or if it does not start.
Repeats Kad's reachability test (TCP and UDP), like the eMule command. It answers at once (202): the result is read from /kad (tcp_firewalled, udp_firewalled, udp_verified). 409 if Kad is off.
Stops Kad (saves the contacts). It does not fail if Kad was already stopped.

get.description: All the preferences managed by the API, as a flat key/value object (see APIDOC.md for the list and the meaning).

patch.description: Body: only the keys to change. Everything is checked first: if a key is unknown or a value is not valid, nothing changes (422). "saved" says whether they were written to the profile: a daemon started with temporary identity or ports changes them only in memory. "restart_required" lists the changed keys that take effect from the next start.

422.description: Unknown key, invalid type or limits

get.description: Category 0 ("all") is always there.

post.description: At least "title" is needed. It is saved at once in Category.ini.

patch.description: Only the given fields. Category 0 changes neither name nor folder.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Category number (0 = all)

delete.description: The downloads of that category go back to "all". 0 cannot be deleted; the following ids shift down by one.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Category number (0 = all)

get.description: The list of servers (server.met).

post.description: Body: "address" (address:port, a DNS name also works), "name", "priority" (low, normal, high), "static". server.met is rewritten. 409 if it is already there; 422 if the address is not allowed (local, 0.0.0.0 or filtered).

delete.description: Removes every server (eMule: "Remove all") and rewrites server.met empty. A connection attempt is stopped; the connection to the current server stays until it closes.

patch.description: Priority, fixed server (static) and/or name. server.met is rewritten.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: address:port of the server (e.g. 176.123.5.89:4725)

delete.summary: Remove a server from the list
delete.description: If it is the connected server, it is disconnected first. server.met is rewritten.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: address:port of the server (e.g. 176.123.5.89:4725)

post.description: With "address": "ip:port" it connects to that server; without a body (or without address) to any one in the list. It answers at once (202): the status is read from /status.
Closes the connection and stops the attempts.

get.description: WebSocket connection (Upgrade) with the token in ?token=. JSON messages {type, data}: stats, server.state, kad.state, download.added|updated|removed, search.results, log. See APIDOC.md, section 6.
The OpenAPI description of the API, served by the daemon.
